FOLLOW TRACE

F001 FOLLOW: Changing _save_round_json() and _save_checkpoint() to call _atomic_write_json() means durability behavior becomes consistent with signal_complete(). Downstream impacts:
- _save_round_json() currently documents normal save only; no semantic change needed.
- _save_checkpoint() now benefits handle_model_failure(), persist(), and any future callers automatically.
- _atomic_write_json() itself still lacks directory fsync after rename, analogous to the already-known save_json durability limitation in verification_chain.py; I am not reopening that same class here for insect_brain because it was not fixed there, but the helper remains weaker than full crash-consistent rename durability.

F002 FOLLOW: Restoring immune_response into RoundRecord affects:
- run_immune_pipeline(): when called after recovery, it overwrites the last round's immune_response as before.
- Any code that introspects rr.immune_response after load_checkpoint() now sees a dict/string payload, not a typed ImmuneResponse object. That preserves data but changes type. If typed access is required, a separate deserialiser is needed. No such deserialiser exists in the current file, so exact type restoration is not possible without additional schema work.

F003 FOLLOW: Hardening verify_record() removes an uncaught-exception path used by _cli_verify_record(). Adding sealed_body validation in load_json() also affects:
- _cli_verify_chain(), _cli_verify_record(), _cli_show_head(), _cli_seal_epoch(), _cli_prove_record() may now fail earlier on malformed JSON with ValueError instead of loading and failing later. That is desirable fail-closed behavior.
- verify_chain() continues to provide aggregate diagnostics for already-loaded in-memory malformed records; no incompatibility created.

F004 FOLLOW: Tightening manifest verification affects cytotoxic_t_cell_v2_shadow():
- test_severity will drop for unscoped or malformed grep steps, reducing confidence inflation.
- Existing CT v2 outputs that only report a bare grep pattern string may now produce lower confidence until the prompt/schema is updated to emit structured args including paths. That exposes a new alignment issue: _CT_V2_FALSIFIER_PROMPT should instruct the agent to record grep paths explicitly, otherwise many valid searches will be undercounted.

F005 FOLLOW: Escaping descriptions affects both CT prompt builders only.
- No downstream parser changes are required because the models consume prompt text, not XML parsing code.
- If prior experiments relied on literal raw description text inside prompts for exact matching, those comparisons will change. That is acceptable because the security boundary claim otherwise remains false.

F006 FOLLOW: Narrowing directed message selection to exactly prev_round affects relay_directed():
- Models will no longer receive same-round messages if state.current_round has already been advanced by persist(). That matches the documented protocol.
- Historical diagnostics via get_directed_messages_for_model() remain unchanged.
- If any orchestrator depended on replaying older unanswered messages automatically, that behavior stops; such replay is not documented and should be explicit if desired.

F007 FOLLOW: Persisting metrics after compute_metrics() mutation affects:
- round_XX.json and checkpoint.json schemas already include metrics, so no schema change.
- More disk writes occur, one per compute_metrics() call. If compute_metrics() is called repeatedly for the same round, persistence cost increases. A debounce or dirty-check could optimise this later, but correctness requires immediate persistence.
- load_checkpoint() already restores rr.get("metrics", {}), so this fix closes the persistence loop fully.

F008 FOLLOW: Type validation in _normalize_timestamp() affects append_record():
- Non-string timestamp callers now get ValueError, which main() already catches and reports cleanly.
- No downstream functional changes for valid strings. This fix only regularises invalid-input handling.
